arguments.expected_measurable_effect: On the next complete execution of the single changed candidate, compared with baseline-replay: the final holding-window tip speed (scheduled 0.05 s window, same 0.02 m/s speed limit) differs measurably from the recorded 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s band, reported separately from terminal reach (terminal tip error against the 0.01 m tolerance), holding-window position error (0.01 m limit), and computation (per-update wall time and deadline misses). A reduction, an increase, or no measurable change are each informative for this bounded experiment.
arguments.rationale: Accepted diagnosis (bound baseline-replay inventory, 35 retained updates, single execution): terminal reach is recorded as passed with terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m against the 0.01 m reach tolerance [fff8ec664f4de, f12f1083f9849], but terminal tip speed is recorded 0.6351726092425104 m/s [ffad04d70b19c] and the final holding window (6 selected samples, t 0.3-0.35 s [fa54c1ae23d4d, f5cdbebaa75dc]) records tip speed 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s [f952823a6555c, ff296c4b0c654] against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit [f4ab3008c7e24], with holding position and sampled settling both recorded as failed [f5ba2ab7e1107, f641da2506e2e]. The retained recipe records terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 [f43a886f15dbe] and holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 [f7264b775e0bb], so the objective that produced this record contains no tip-speed cost term at all. Hypothesis: the recorded deviation is concentrated in tip speed, and an absent tip-speed penalty is a plausible contributor to that deviation, so positive values on these two terms should drive the sampled tip-speed band toward the 0.02 m/s settling limit. Relevance of this weight to this observation: these are the only two editable handles acting on squared tip speed, they are currently exactly zero so any positive value is an effective delta, and tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s, scheduling and structure remain unchanged. Expected effects, stated separately: holding speed (primary) - the scheduled holding-node sum should lower window tip speed below its current 0.635-1.581 m/s band; terminal reach - possible small degradation, since a terminal braking term can move the final approach while the terminal position margin under the 0.01 m tolerance is limited; holding position - secondary, plausibly improved if reduced speed reduces overshoot, but could be unchanged; computation - the objective gains terms and may raise iterations/nonconvexity, and nothing in the retained record indicates per-update wall time (already ~17 s against a 0.01 s control period [fb97841323574, ff74842fa741e, fc06e64bbb5d7]) would improve. Value selection is by mechanism only, since raw weight magnitudes are not calibrated against cost contributions or scaling; 0.01 on each weight is a bounded first choice, not a computed optimum, and no raw scalar objective will be compared across weights. Possible adverse effects: eroded reach margin, worse solve cost or deadline behaviour, and, with no causal attribution available, a null result cannot be read as proof that the term is irrelevant. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: holding-window tip speed still ~0.6-1.6 m/s after the change; reach error crossing 0.01 m; terminal tip speed still far above 0.02 m/s; or deadline misses and per-update wall times materially worse than the baseline record. All other scientific fields remain fixed. A local 0.01 s projected-model comparison is omitted, not because it is unavailable but because a <=10 ms horizon probe cannot represent the 0.05 s settling window or closed-loop settling, so it would test neither the failing window quantity nor this hypothesis.

arguments.reasoning: Deferral, not adoption. The single authorized control change (holding_tip_speed_weight raised from the recorded baseline 0.0 [fe5f206322c2f] to 0.01 [ffa86380899d7], with terminal_tip_speed_weight also set positive [fdb85d027047b]) executed as a complete, valid run (complete true [fff684fc661de]; evaluation_validity 'valid' [ff37e5e0576b6]; solver_error_count 0 [ff1ac3503e552]; no force-bound violation [f008bb9364acd]; status 'evaluated' [fdd292670d74f]). It nevertheless lost the baseline's reach-only success (candidate terminal reach passed false [fb2196608130b] versus baseline official reach-task success true [ffee5636d7761]) and moved the ranked physical metrics in the worse direction: candidate holding-window maximum error 0.06521673847872775 m [fb551b0074893] with candidate-minus-baseline delta +0.00707863419299519 m [fd95239e6261c], and candidate sampled-settling maximum speed 2.2241210494240513 m/s [ffc6930742d22] versus the baseline holding-window maximum 1.5810152739742807 m/s [ff296c4b0c654]. Across both runs the 0.01 m position limit [f96748bb61be2], the 0.02 m/s speed limit [fec74be98dd03] and the 0.05 s settling window [fd898a5a0c311] remain unmet (sampled settling not passed [ff9225bf3aa43]; real-time not demonstrated [ff9345a5f7bef]), and the 10 ms control period [fd007fcdf7be2] is still missed on all 35 updates in each run [fc09ef600a821]. Those limits are reported as threshold observations, not as causes. No causal attribution is available: control_snapshots.json (full warm plans, optimizer iteration traces) is not retained, the candidate has no per-update inventory in this context, and a bounded projected-model probe of at most 0.01 s effective horizon cannot explain an entire settling failure, so any link between the computation record and the holding-window excursions stays at temporal co-occurrence. A valid completed workflow is therefore distinct from demonstrated design improvement, and no further parameter value or candidate is authorized.

recommendations.rationale: The single authorized parameter change (holding_tip_speed_weight and terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.01) executed as a complete valid run and measured as a physical pareto worsening on the ranked metrics (candidate holding maximum speed 2.2241210494240513 m/s versus baseline 1.5810152739742807 m/s; candidate-minus-baseline holding maximum error +0.00707863419299519 m) while losing reach-only success; no parameter value is supported from this revision and no further candidate is authorized.

The unresolved mechanism linking the per-update computation record to the holding-window position and speed excursions cannot be tested with the available tools: there is no closed-loop counterfactual replay, control_snapshots.json is not retained, the candidate has no per-update inventory here, and the bounded projected-model probe (effective horizon <= 0.01 s) cannot explain an entire settling failure.

attribution.reason: Reach-only success is true at the last execution sample (terminal error 0.007642608585867386 m below the 0.01 m tolerance) while the 6 sampled rows of the final 0.05 s window include errors 0.04778599698437965 m and 0.019054532266831993 m above the same limit and speeds 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s above the 0.02 m/s limit, and the retained joint reach-plus-holding criterion is false. The pass therefore describes the update-34 endpoint observation only.

Holding position and holding speed are both recorded failed over the final window (errors up to 0.04778599698437965 m in the retained rows, speed up to 1.5810152739742807 m/s), and terminal speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s is far above the 0.02 m/s limit. A terminal position pass does not correspond to settled motion in this record.

The baseline records reach-only success true while joint reach-plus-holding success is false, and the candidate records reach-only success false while holding still fails. The two acceptance levels are distinct in both runs.

The executed candidate raised both tip-speed weights from 0.0 to 0.01 and, in its complete valid execution, recorded a higher holding-window maximum speed (2.2241210494240513 m/s versus 1.5810152739742807 m/s), a higher holding maximum error (candidate-minus-baseline +0.00707863419299519 m) and loss of reach-only success. Every ranked physical metric moved in the worse direction (physical_pareto_worsening); with a single execution this rules out this specific change as an observed improvement without asserting the underlying mechanism.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists in this context, and the runs are recorded in different scopes (35 updates versus 6 window rows; aggregate candidate profile versus baseline window rows). Wall-clock overruns are synchronous and do not establish skipped simulated updates, and the deadline-miss count is the same in both runs although their holding speeds differ, so only temporal co-occurrence is supported.

One complete execution with one seed, compared at aggregate level under a frozen classification, cannot separate weight effects from solver-path differences (converged updates 1 versus 2) or shared model error; shared model errors need not cancel and small differences do not prove input or causal-hypothesis equivalence. Only summary-level candidate results are handed over.

A projected-model probe with an effective horizon of at most 0.01 s cannot explain an entire settling failure, and this revision phase performs no solve or evaluation. It is not the basis of any statement reported here.

Terminal reach covers one endpoint (update 34, t = 0.35 s); holding position and holding speed each cover the 6 retained rows of the final 0.05 s window; computation covers 35 controller updates. Nothing retained promotes them beyond separately scoped, temporally co-occurring observations.

limitations: Coverage as stated: terminal reach is one endpoint observation; holding position and holding speed each cover the 6 retained rows of the final 0.05 s window (t 0.3-0.35 s); computation covers 35 retained controller updates. No whole-trajectory range is asserted.

The frozen classification string physical_pareto_worsening and several candidate-minus-baseline deltas (mean complete update +2.4917310400001185 s, terminal error +0.017799341299716415 m, holding maximum speed +0.6431057754497707 m/s, deadline-miss delta 0, candidate mean complete update 19.755050088565 s) have no displayed catalog handle and are reported from the handed-over campaign_comparison/profile content rather than from a catalog selector.

Not displayed in this context: the candidate execution's own per-update inventory (sampled backend motion, saved projected states, applied tensions, plan selection, solver status); the bound inventory covers the baseline execution only, so candidate comparisons rest on aggregate profile/evaluation/factual results.

Not computable with current tools: causal attribution or closed-loop counterfactual replay (causal_identification is listed as unsupported); the relationship between the computation record and the holding-window excursions is limited to temporal co-occurrence.
Wall-clock misses and overruns are synchronous; they do not inject simulated delay or establish skipped simulated updates, and no simulated-delay claim is made here.
Single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause; the measured candidate change is a pareto worsening, not a trade-off in which one physical metric improved.

Only terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight were eligible for change; that specific change was executed and measured as a worsening, and this phase authorizes no further candidate or saved-state check.
recommended_actions: Advisory: do not adopt the executed change; on the frozen comparison it worsened every ranked physical metric (holding maximum speed 2.2241210494240513 m/s versus baseline 1.5810152739742807 m/s; candidate-minus-baseline holding maximum error +0.00707863419299519 m) and lost reach-only success, so the actual measurements weaken the hypothesis that raising the tip-speed weights improves settling.

Advisory: the relationship between the per-update computation record and the holding-window excursions remains temporal co-occurrence only; a causal statement would first require a closed-loop counterfactual replay capability, retained control_snapshots.json, candidate per-update records, and a probe with an effective horizon longer than the bounded <=0.01 s projected-model probe.

Advisory: the remaining mechanism gap is not closable by another parameter value in this phase; per the phase instruction no further candidate and no saved-state check is authorized, so the deferral disposition stands.
